messages:
sam: Heads-up — planning a config-only rollout in the 22:00-23:00 PT change window tonight. Adjusting routing weights, request timeout, and batching defaults. No model or runtime binary change. Canary at 5% then quick ramp if metrics look good.

deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Starting config-only rollout (id=2156789001). Canary target: 5% of traffic -> pool 'canary-economy'. Changes: routing_policy weights, request_timeout_ms, batch.max_tokens/batch_delay_ms. Will post progress updates here.

jordan: Quick q — any kv-cache warmup or prefix-cache changes that could spike tail latency?

sam: No kv-cache changes. This is just routing + batching + timeout. Expect small perf delta for short requests because batch_delay decreased slightly. Config snippet:

```yaml
canary: 5%
routing_policies:
  - name: prefer-economy
    weight: 0.15
timeouts:
  request_timeout_ms: 6500
batching:
  batch_size: 16
  batch_delay_ms: 12
  max_tokens_per_batch: 4096
```

marta: I'll watch p99 latency, 5xx rate, and queue depth. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/infra/routing-batching (watch panel 3/4). If p99 increases > 20% or 5xx > 0.25% for 5m -> manual rollback. :eyes:

erin: Rollback/runbook? Also want the config hash pinned for quick revert and release notes entry.

sam: Rollback plan: 1) revert to config hash `cfg-2026-02-19-7b3a` via deploy CLI: `redwood deploy config revert cfg-2026-02-19-7b3a --id=2156789001` 2) if that fails, pin routing to previous policy `prefer-economy: 0.05` and increase request_timeout_ms to 8s. I'm adding release-notes blurb now.

deploy-bot: Canary reached 5% after 12m. Metrics: p99 latency +2ms, avg latency -3ms, 5xx delta +0.00%. Approving roll to 50%.

marta: Moving to 50% — watching for next 30m. Will alert on Slack #oncall if thresholds breached.

sam: For release notes: "Config-only: routing/batching tuning to reduce cost per request and tighten short-request tail. No model/runtime changes. Canary success -> progressive rollout." Adding to changelog and tagging internal docs.

erin: Thanks — tagging @support for FYI. If anything odd, we'll execute the revert command above. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Rollout status: 50% -> ongoing. Will post final status when at 100% or if rollback triggered.
